title: UDLF deployment config — Microsoft Sentinel
description: Optional, opt-in sub-schema for the `config` block of a UDLF deployment whose `platform` is `sentinel`. Covers Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules: schedule, trigger, alert presentation, incident grouping and entity mappings. The KQL query is not here — it lives in `detection_content` like any other language variant. Neither are the fields UDLF already owns: maturity and runtime behaviour come from `lifecycle` and `mode`, authorship from `metadata.authors`, and each target workspace is its own deployment entry rather than a tenant list. Vendor-assigned rule ids are absent too, because UDLF is desired-state only — reconciling against what is actually deployed is the deployer's job. ATT&CK techniques come from the top-level `threat` block, but `alert.tactics` is modelled here because Sentinel spells its tactics its own way (`CommandAndControl`). Every field notes the Sentinel API property it maps to. This schema is NOT referenced by the UDLF core schema; apply it separately when you want the block validated.

allOf.$comment: Near-real-time rules are hard-coded to run every minute over the preceding minute and alert on first match, so frequency, lookback and trigger are all meaningless — Sentinel rejects them. The inverse (a scheduled rule requires frequency, lookback and trigger) is left to the deployer, since a partially-authored UDLF config is legitimate and the deployer fills the rest.

schema.description: Self-identifying sub-schema version for this config block, so this file can version independently of UDLF core.

template.description: Provenance of the Sentinel gallery template this rule was created from. Populating it lets Sentinel's UI track rules back to their template.

uuid.description: Template rule UUID, findable in the Sentinel rule repository or analyticsrules.exchange. Maps to `alertRuleTemplateName`.

version.description: Template version in a.b.c form. Maps to `templateVersion`.

scheduling.description: How often the rule runs and how far back it looks. Sentinel supports 5 minutes to 14 days for both.

nrt.description: Run as a Near Real Time rule: fixed one-minute cadence over the preceding minute, alerting on first match. Note that Sentinel cannot convert a rule between NRT and scheduled — switching means deleting the rule and deploying a new one under a fresh id.

frequency.description: How often the query runs, as `Nd`/`Nh`/`Nm`. Sentinel allows 5 minutes to 14 days. Maps to `queryFrequency`.

lookback.description: How far back the query searches, up to 14 days. Maps to `queryPeriod`.

trigger.description: How many query results are needed to raise an alert. Not valid on NRT rules.

threshold.description: Result count the operator compares against. Maps to `triggerThreshold`.

alert.description: Alert presentation and incident behaviour. The title/description/severity fields override what Sentinel would otherwise derive from the detection, and support `{{columnName}}` substitution so one rule can raise differently-shaped alerts.

create_incident.description: Create incidents from alerts this rule raises. Maps to `incidentConfiguration.createIncident`.

suppression.description: How long to wait after firing before the rule may fire again, 5 minutes to 1 day. Use boolean `false` to disable suppression entirely. Maps to `suppressionDuration`.

title.description: Alert display name, up to 256 characters with at most 3 `{{columnName}}` placeholders. Overrides the detection title. Maps to `alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat`.

description.description: Alert description, up to 5000 characters with at most 3 `{{columnName}}` placeholders. Overrides `detection_context.description`. Maps to `alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat`.

severity.description: Severity to raise the alert with. Overrides `detection_context.severity` for this deployment.

tactics.description: ATT&CK tactics as Sentinel spells them — note `CommandAndControl` rather than the ATT&CK display form, plus ICS-only values. Kept here rather than derived from the top-level `threat` block because the vocabulary is Sentinel's own; a deployer may still generate it from `threat.attack` when omitted.

custom_details.description: Surface query columns as named key/value pairs on the alert. Maps to `customDetails`.

key.description: Field name shown on the alert. No whitespace.

column.description: Query result column supplying the value.

dynamic_properties.description: Override built-in alert properties from query columns. Maps to `alertDetailsOverride.alertDynamicProperties`.

property.description: The V3 alert property to override.

column.description: Query result column supplying the value. Maps to `value`.

grouping.description: How query results become alerts, and how alerts become incidents.

allOf.$comment: Sentinel needs a window and a matching method before it can group alerts into incidents.

event.description: `SingleAlert` groups all query results into one alert; `AlertPerResult` raises one alert per result. Maps to `eventGroupingSettings.aggregationKind`.

alert.description: Group alerts from this rule into a single incident. Sentinel caps an incident at 150 alerts; beyond that it opens a new incident with the same details.

reopen_closed_incidents.description: Re-open a closed matching incident instead of opening a new one. Maps to `...groupingConfiguration.reopenClosedIncident`.

grouping_lookback.description: Only group alerts raised within this window. Maps to `...groupingConfiguration.lookbackDuration`.

matching.description: `AllEntities` groups when every entity matches (recommended); `AnyAlert` groups everything this rule raises; `Selected` groups on the `group_by_*` lists below. Maps to `...groupingConfiguration.matchingMethod`.

group_by_entities.description: Entity types to group on when `matching` is `Selected`. Only entities mapped by this rule may be used. Maps to `...groupingConfiguration.groupByEntities`.

group_by_alert_details.description: Alert details to group on when `matching` is `Selected`. Maps to `...groupingConfiguration.groupByAlertDetails`.

group_by_custom_details.description: Custom detail keys to group on when `matching` is `Selected`. Only keys declared in `alert.custom_details` may be used. Maps to `...groupingConfiguration.groupByCustomDetails`.

entities.description: Entity mappings — how query columns become the accounts, hosts, IPs and so on that Sentinel builds investigation graphs and automation from. Each entity type accepts its own identifier set and requires at least one strong identifier. Maps to `entityMappings`.

mappings.description: Field mappings for the Account entity. At least one must use a strong identifier (Sid, Name, FullName, AadUserId, PUID, ObjectGuid) — Sentinel cannot construct the entity otherwise.

identifier.description: Which Account attribute this column supplies.

column.description: Query result column holding the value. Must exist in the query output.

exclusions.description: Tuning exclusions appended to the deployed query in order, each documented with a reason. A per-endpoint exclusion is a separate deployment entry in UDLF, so there is no tenant field here.

reason.description: Why this exclusion exists. Required so tuning decisions stay auditable.

let.description: KQL `let` bindings emitted before the exclusion query and referenceable from it. Values are inserted verbatim.

query.description: KQL appended to the base query.

advanced.description: Escape hatch for Sentinel API properties this sub-schema does not model. Passed through verbatim, so keys must match the API exactly. Prefer a modelled field where one exists — anything here is unvalidated and invisible to tooling.
